# assistant-ui

> Production AI chat UIs in React with streaming, attachments and tool UIs.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tier | **recommended** |
| AI-readiness | **90/100** |
| Maintainer | assistant-ui |
| Platforms | web |
| Frameworks | react |
| Styling | tailwind |
| Good for | ai-app, chat |
| License | MIT |
| GitHub stars | 13.0k |
| npm weekly downloads | 2.9M (`@assistant-ui/react`) |
| Last activity | 2026-11-04 |
| Docs | https://www.assistant-ui.com |
| Source | https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui |

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://www.assistant-ui.com/llms.txt
- **llms-full.txt:** https://www.assistant-ui.com/llms-full.txt
- **MCP server:**
  - in-repo package: https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/tree/HEAD/apps/docs (see its README for setup)
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/blob/HEAD/packages/ui/src/components/react/assistant-ui/utils/tokens.ts
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/blob/HEAD/.claude/skills/change-review/SKILL.md

## Consider an alternative if
- the project does not use (or cannot add) Tailwind CSS.

## Install
```bash
npx assistant-ui@latest create     # new app
npx assistant-ui@latest init       # existing shadcn/ui app
```

## What you get
Composable primitives (Thread, Composer, Message, ActionBar) with runtimes for the AI SDK, LangGraph, Mastra or a custom backend; streaming, attachments, tool-call UIs.

## Agent tips
- Styled defaults follow shadcn/ui theming; use with a shadcn base for the rest of the app.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Score breakdown
| Capability | Points |
|---|---|
| Official MCP server (agent can query components/docs live) | 20/20 |
| llms.txt on the docs site | 15/15 |
| llms-full.txt (whole docs as one markdown file) | 5/5 |
| Machine-readable design tokens in the repo | 15/15 |
| Typed component API (TypeScript / Swift / Kotlin / Dart / C#) | 10/10 |
| Registry / CLI install of component source (e.g. shadcn registry) | 10/10 |
| Agent instructions in the repo (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, cursor rules, skills) | 5/5 |
| Storybook / live, inspectable examples | 0/5 |
| Figma Code Connect (design ↔ code mapping) | 0/5 |
| Accessibility guidance shipped with the source | 5/5 |
| Dedicated documentation site | 5/5 |

Quality gate: activity **active**; traction via stars, npm.

_Data refreshed 2026-11-05. Source: https://kindavishal.github.io/ai-ready-design-systems/systems/assistant-ui.md_

# HeroUI (formerly NextUI)

> Good-looking consumer and SaaS React apps on Tailwind with animations built in.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tier | **recommended** |
| AI-readiness | **95/100** |
| Maintainer | HeroUI |
| Platforms | web |
| Frameworks | react |
| Styling | tailwind |
| Good for | consumer, saas, marketing, startup-mvp |
| License | Apache-2.0 |
| GitHub stars | 31.1k |
| npm weekly downloads | 1.2M (`@heroui/react`) |
| Last activity | 2026-10-30 |
| Docs | https://www.heroui.com |
| Source | https://github.com/heroui-inc/heroui |

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://www.heroui.com/llms.txt
- **llms-full.txt:** https://www.heroui.com/llms-full.txt
- **MCP server:**
  - npm package `@heroui/react-mcp`
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"heroui":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@heroui/react-mcp"]}}}
    ```
  - in-repo package: https://github.com/heroui-inc/heroui/tree/HEAD/apps/docs (see its README for setup)
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/heroui-inc/heroui/blob/HEAD/packages/styles/themes/default/variables.css
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/heroui-inc/heroui/blob/HEAD/AGENTS.md

## Consider an alternative if
- the project does not use (or cannot add) Tailwind CSS.

## Install
```bash
npx heroui-cli@latest init        # new project
# existing app: npm install @heroui/react framer-motion   (Tailwind required)
```
Follow the Tailwind plugin step in the docs (v4: `@plugin './hero.ts'` in your CSS).

## Setup
```tsx
import { HeroUIProvider } from '@heroui/react';
<HeroUIProvider>{/* app */}</HeroUIProvider>
```

## Theme it to a brand
Themes are defined in the `heroui()` Tailwind plugin (`themes: { light: { colors: { primary: { DEFAULT: '#…' } } } }`).

## Agent tips
- MCP server: `npx -y @heroui/react-mcp` ; docs index at `https://www.heroui.com/llms.txt`.
- Check whether the project is on HeroUI v2 or v3 before copying examples — the APIs differ.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

# shadcn/ui

> Modern SaaS and AI apps on React/Next.js + Tailwind where you want to own and restyle component source.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tier | **recommended** |
| AI-readiness | **80/100** |
| Maintainer | shadcn (Vercel) (org-backed) |
| Platforms | web |
| Frameworks | react |
| Styling | tailwind |
| Good for | saas, startup-mvp, dashboard, marketing, ai-app, devtools |
| License | MIT |
| GitHub stars | 127.4k |
| npm weekly downloads | 17.3M (`shadcn`) |
| Last activity | 2026-11-04 |
| Docs | https://ui.shadcn.com |
| Source | https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui |

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://ui.shadcn.com/llms.txt
- **MCP server:**
  - `npx shadcn@latest mcp`
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"shadcn-ui":{"command":"npx","args":["shadcn@latest","mcp"]}}}
    ```
- **Theming tokens:** Theme is CSS variables (globals.css) generated per registry theme; see ui.shadcn.com/docs/theming
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/HEAD/apps/v4/AGENTS.md

## Consider an alternative if
- the project does not use (or cannot add) Tailwind CSS.

## Install
```bash
npx shadcn@latest init          # in an existing Next.js / Vite / React Router / Astro app with Tailwind
npx shadcn@latest add button card dialog form input table sidebar
```
New project: `npx shadcn@latest init` offers templates; or start from `npx create-next-app@latest` first.

## How it works
Components are copied into your repo (`components/ui/*`) — you own and edit the source. Config lives in `components.json`. Built on Radix (or Base UI) primitives + Tailwind.

## Theme it to a brand
- Edit the CSS variables in `app/globals.css` (`--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--radius`, …) for `:root` and `.dark`.
- Pick a base theme at init, or generate one at ui.shadcn.com/themes and paste the variables.
- Fonts: set in your layout and map to `--font-sans`.

## Agent tips
- Run `npx shadcn@latest mcp init` (or add `npx shadcn@latest mcp` to your MCP client) so you can search and install registry items directly.
- Use **blocks** (`npx shadcn@latest add dashboard-01 sidebar-07 login-03`) to scaffold whole screens, then edit.
- Never hand-write a component that exists in the registry; `add` it.
- Charts: `add chart` (Recharts). Forms: `add form` (react-hook-form + zod).

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Score breakdown
| Capability | Points |
|---|---|
| Official MCP server (agent can query components/docs live) | 20/20 |
| llms.txt on the docs site | 15/15 |
| llms-full.txt (whole docs as one markdown file) | 0/5 |
| Machine-readable design tokens in the repo | 15/15 |

# Mantine

> Full-featured React apps needing 100+ components plus hooks, forms, dates, charts and notifications out of the box.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tier | **recommended** |
| AI-readiness | **85/100** |
| Maintainer | Mantine |
| Platforms | web |
| Frameworks | react |
| Styling | css-modules |
| Good for | saas, dashboard, admin, startup-mvp |
| License | MIT |
| GitHub stars | 31.9k |
| npm weekly downloads | 3.5M (`@mantine/core`) |
| Last activity | 2026-11-04 |
| Docs | https://mantine.dev |
| Source | https://github.com/mantinedev/mantine |

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://mantine.dev/llms.txt
- **llms-full.txt:** https://mantine.dev/llms-full.txt
- **MCP server:**
  - in-repo package: https://github.com/mantinedev/mantine/tree/HEAD/packages/@mantine/mcp-server (see its README for setup)
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/mantinedev/mantine/blob/HEAD/apps/mantine.dev/src/styles/variables.css
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/mantinedev/mantine/blob/HEAD/AGENTS.md


## Install
```bash
npm install @mantine/core @mantine/hooks
# extras as needed: @mantine/form @mantine/dates dayjs @mantine/notifications @mantine/charts recharts @mantine/modals
```
Requires `postcss-preset-mantine` + `postcss-simple-vars` (see Getting started) and `import '@mantine/core/styles.css'`.

## Setup
```tsx
import { MantineProvider, createTheme } from '@mantine/core';
const theme = createTheme({ primaryColor: 'indigo', fontFamily: 'Inter, sans-serif', defaultRadius: 'md' });
<MantineProvider theme={theme} defaultColorScheme="auto">{/* app */}</MantineProvider>
```
Next.js: add `ColorSchemeScript` in `<head>`.

## Agent tips
- Read `https://mantine.dev/llms.txt`; Mantine also publishes an MCP server (`@mantine/mcp-server`).
- Prefer Mantine's own `AppShell`, `useForm`, `notifications` over third-party libs — it keeps one visual language.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

# Chakra UI

> Accessible, themeable React apps with style props; fast to brand.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tier | **recommended** |
| AI-readiness | **85/100** |
| Maintainer | Chakra UI |
| Platforms | web |
| Frameworks | react |
| Styling | css-in-js |
| Good for | saas, startup-mvp, consumer, marketing |
| License | MIT |
| GitHub stars | 40.7k |
| npm weekly downloads | 2.1M (`@chakra-ui/react`) |
| Last activity | 2026-11-03 |
| Docs | https://chakra-ui.com |
| Source | https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui |

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://chakra-ui.com/llms.txt
- **llms-full.txt:** https://chakra-ui.com/llms-full.txt
- **MCP server:**
  - npm package `@chakra-ui/react-mcp`
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"chakra-ui":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@chakra-ui/react-mcp"]}}}
    ```
  - in-repo package: https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui/tree/HEAD/apps/mcp (see its README for setup)
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui/blob/HEAD/apps/www/public/r/theme/tokens.json
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui/blob/HEAD/CLAUDE.md

## Consider an alternative if
- you need zero-runtime styling or heavy React Server Components use — check the docs for RSC support.

## Install
```bash
npm install @chakra-ui/react @emotion/react
npx @chakra-ui/cli snippet add      # adds provider, color-mode and other snippets to your repo
```

## Setup
```tsx
import { Provider } from '@/components/ui/provider';   // generated by the CLI
export default function RootLayout({ children }) { return <html suppressHydrationWarning><body><Provider>{children}</Provider></body></html>; }
```

## Theme it to a brand
v3 uses `createSystem(defaultConfig, { theme: { tokens: { colors: { brand: { 500: { value: '#…' } } } }, semanticTokens: {…} } })` and passes it to `ChakraProvider value={system}`. Generate types with `npx @chakra-ui/cli typegen`.

## Agent tips
- MCP server: `npx -y @chakra-ui/react-mcp` (component props, examples, v2→v3 migration).
- `https://chakra-ui.com/llms.txt` has per-component docs. Chakra v3 API differs from v2 — don't use v2 examples.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

```bash
npm install @ark-ui/react
```

- Design tokens live in the repo (e.g. `website/src/theme/tokens`); map brand colours/typography onto these rather than hard-coding values.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

# Quasar

> Quasar by Quasar.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tier | **recommended** |
| AI-readiness | **75/100** |
| Maintainer | Quasar |
| Platforms | web, ios, android, desktop |
| Frameworks | vue |
| Styling | css |
| Good for | admin, hybrid-app, mobile |
| License | MIT |
| GitHub stars | 27.2k |
| npm weekly downloads | 478.1k (`quasar`) |
| Last activity | 2026-10-19 |
| Docs | https://quasar.dev |
| Source | https://github.com/quasarframework/quasar |

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://quasar.dev/llms.txt
- **MCP server:**
  - in-repo package: https://github.com/quasarframework/quasar/tree/HEAD/mcp/README.md (see its README for setup)
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/quasarframework/quasar/blob/HEAD/docs/build/mcp/output/tokens.js
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/quasarframework/quasar/blob/HEAD/.claude/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md


## Install
```bash
npm init quasar
```
One Vue codebase → SPA, SSR, PWA, mobile (Capacitor/Cordova) and desktop (Electron).

## Theme it to a brand
`quasar.config` → `framework.config.brand` or Sass variables (`$primary`, `$secondary`) in `src/css/quasar.variables.scss`.

## Agent tips
- The repo ships an MCP server (see `mcp/` in the repo) for component lookup.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Score breakdown

# Nuxt UI

> Vue / Nuxt SaaS and marketing sites on Tailwind, with templates and dashboard blocks.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tier | **recommended** |
| AI-readiness | **75/100** |
| Maintainer | NuxtLabs (Vercel) (org-backed) |
| Platforms | web |
| Frameworks | vue, nuxt |
| Styling | tailwind |
| Good for | saas, startup-mvp, marketing, dashboard |
| License | MIT |
| GitHub stars | 7.1k |
| npm weekly downloads | 985.2k (`@nuxt/ui`) |
| Last activity | 2026-11-04 |
| Docs | https://ui.nuxt.com |
| Source | https://github.com/nuxt/ui |

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://ui.nuxt.com/llms.txt
- **llms-full.txt:** https://ui.nuxt.com/llms-full.txt
- **MCP server:**
  - remote server https://ui.nuxt.com/mcp
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"nuxt-ui":{"type":"http","url":"https://ui.nuxt.com/mcp"}}}
    ```
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/nuxt/ui/blob/HEAD/docs/app/utils/theme/tokens.ts
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/nuxt/ui/blob/HEAD/AGENTS.md

## Consider an alternative if
- the project does not use (or cannot add) Tailwind CSS.

## Install
```bash
npm create nuxt@latest -- -t ui          # new Nuxt project with Nuxt UI
# existing: npx nuxt module add ui   then  @import "tailwindcss"; @import "@nuxt/ui";  in main.css
```
Plain Vue (Vite) is supported too via the `@nuxt/ui/vite` plugin.

## Setup
Wrap the app in `<UApp>` (provides toasts, tooltips, overlays).

## Theme it to a brand
`app.config.ts`: `ui: { colors: { primary: 'indigo', neutral: 'zinc' } }`; per-component `ui` slots override classes. Tailwind `@theme` for custom colour scales.

## Agent tips
- Remote MCP server: `https://ui.nuxt.com/mcp`; docs at `https://ui.nuxt.com/llms.txt`.
- Starter templates (dashboard, SaaS, landing, docs, chat) exist — start from one.

## Build checklist (any system)

5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

# Material UI (MUI)

> Feature-rich React apps and admin tools that benefit from Material Design and a huge component set (incl. MUI X data grid).

| | |
|---|---|
| Tier | **recommended** |
| AI-readiness | **60/100** |
| Maintainer | MUI (org-backed) |
| Platforms | web |
| Frameworks | react |
| Styling | css-in-js |
| Good for | enterprise, saas, dashboard, admin |
| License | MIT |
| GitHub stars | 99.3k |
| npm weekly downloads | 13.6M (`@mui/material`) |
| Last activity | 2026-11-03 |
| Docs | https://mui.com/material-ui/ |
| Source | https://github.com/mui/material-ui |

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://mui.com/material-ui/llms.txt
- **MCP server:**
  - npm package `@mui/mcp`
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"mui":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@mui/mcp"]}}}
    ```
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/mui/material-ui/blob/HEAD/.agents/skills/material-ui-review/SKILL.md

## Consider an alternative if
- you need zero-runtime styling or heavy React Server Components use — check the docs for RSC support.

## Install
```bash
npm install @mui/material @emotion/react @emotion/styled @mui/icons-material
# optional: npm install @mui/x-data-grid @mui/x-date-pickers @mui/x-charts
```

## Setup
```tsx
import { ThemeProvider, createTheme, CssBaseline } from '@mui/material';
const theme = createTheme({ cssVariables: true, colorSchemes: { light: true, dark: true },
  palette: { primary: { main: '#4F46E5' } }, shape: { borderRadius: 10 },
  typography: { fontFamily: 'Inter, sans-serif' } });
export default function App() { return <ThemeProvider theme={theme}><CssBaseline />{/* app */}</ThemeProvider>; }
```
Next.js App Router: also install `@mui/material-nextjs` and wrap in `AppRouterCacheProvider`.

## Theme it to a brand
All brand decisions go in `createTheme` (palette, typography, shape, `components` overrides). Avoid per-component `sx` colour literals — use `theme.palette.*`.

## Agent tips
- Add the MCP server: `npx -y @mui/mcp@latest` — gives exact, versioned docs and code samples.
- Read `https://mui.com/material-ui/llms.txt` for the component index.
- Data-heavy UI: MUI X Data Grid (MIT tier) instead of building tables by hand.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

# React Spectrum / React Aria

> Best-in-class accessibility and internationalisation; React Aria for custom-branded systems, Spectrum for Adobe-style tools.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tier | **recommended** |
| AI-readiness | **60/100** |
| Maintainer | Adobe (org-backed) |
| Platforms | web |
| Frameworks | react |
| Styling | headless (headless) |
| Good for | enterprise, accessibility-critical, creative-tools, custom-brand |
| License | Apache-2.0 |
| GitHub stars | 16.0k |
| npm weekly downloads | 8.3M (`react-aria-components`) |
| Last activity | 2026-11-05 |
| Docs | https://react-spectrum.adobe.com |
| Source | https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum |

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/llms.txt
- MCP server: none found
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/HEAD/packages/@react-spectrum/s2/style/tokens.ts
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/HEAD/.claude/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md

## Consider an alternative if
- you want a finished visual style out of the box — this is headless; you supply all styling.

## Install
```bash
npm install react-aria-components          # unstyled, accessible — bring your own styles (Tailwind works well)
# Adobe-styled: npm install @adobe/react-spectrum   (Spectrum 2: @react-spectrum/s2)
```

## Setup
React Aria Components need no provider; style via `className` (render props expose states: `isHovered`, `isFocusVisible`, `isSelected`). Use the Tailwind plugin `tailwindcss-react-aria-components` for state variants.

## When to choose which
- **React Aria**: you need a custom brand with best-in-class a11y + i18n (date pickers, comboboxes, drag & drop, tables).
- **React Spectrum**: Adobe-style creative/pro tools.

## Agent tips
- The docs have copy-paste Tailwind and vanilla CSS starter kits — start from those rather than styling from zero.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

> Framework-agnostic Tailwind component classes with many themes; great for quick MVPs in any stack.

## Install (Tailwind v4)
```bash
npm install -D daisyui@latest
```
```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@plugin "daisyui" { themes: light --default, dark --prefersdark; }
```

## How it works
Semantic class names (`btn btn-primary`, `card`, `modal`) on plain HTML — works with any framework or none.

## Theme it to a brand
Define a custom theme with `@plugin "daisyui/theme" { name: "brand"; --color-primary: oklch(...); --radius-box: 1rem; }` or use the theme generator on daisyui.com.

## Agent tips
- `https://daisyui.com/llms.txt` is a compact, complete class reference — load it before writing markup.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.

5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- you need zero-runtime styling or heavy React Server Components use — check the docs for RSC support.

## Install
```bash
npm create tamagui@latest          # starter monorepo: Expo + Next.js sharing UI
# existing: npm install tamagui @tamagui/config
```

## Setup
```tsx
import { TamaguiProvider, createTamagui } from 'tamagui';
import { defaultConfig } from '@tamagui/config/v4';
const config = createTamagui(defaultConfig);
<TamaguiProvider config={config} defaultTheme="light">{/* app */}</TamaguiProvider>
```

## Agent tips
- Tokens and themes are typed in the config — use `$tokens` (`bg="$background"`, `p="$4"`) not raw values.
- Add the compiler plugin (Next/Vite/Metro) for production performance.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.

5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://react.fluentui.dev/llms.txt
- MCP server: none found
- **Design tokens:** https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui/blob/HEAD/packages/react-components/babel-preset-storybook-full-source/src/__fixtures__/storybook-stories-fullsource-with-tokens/css-module-with-tokens/tokens.css
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui/blob/HEAD/.agents/skills/assign-prs/SKILL.md

## Consider an alternative if
- you are not building inside the microsoft ecosystem — its visual language signals that brand.
- you need zero-runtime styling or heavy React Server Components use — check the docs for RSC support.

## Install
```bash
npm install @fluentui/react-components @fluentui/react-icons
```

## Setup
```tsx
import { FluentProvider, webLightTheme, createLightTheme } from '@fluentui/react-components';
<FluentProvider theme={webLightTheme}>{/* app */}</FluentProvider>
```
Brand: build a 16-step `BrandVariants` ramp and call `createLightTheme(brand)` / `createDarkTheme(brand)`. Use `makeStyles` + `tokens` for custom styling.

## Agent tips
- Use v9 (`@fluentui/react-components`), not v8 (`@fluentui/react`) — they are different libraries.
- Teams apps: use `teamsLightTheme` / `teamsDarkTheme`.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

| Last activity | 2026-11-05 |
| Docs | https://ant.design |
| Source | https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design |

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://ant.design/llms.txt
- **llms-full.txt:** https://ant.design/llms-full.txt
- MCP server: none found
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/HEAD/.agents/skills/changelog-collect/SKILL.md

## Consider an alternative if
- you need zero-runtime styling or heavy React Server Components use — check the docs for RSC support.

## Install
```bash
npm install antd @ant-design/icons
# Next.js App Router: npm install @ant-design/nextjs-registry
```

## Setup
```tsx
import { ConfigProvider, App as AntApp, theme } from 'antd';
<ConfigProvider theme={{ token: { colorPrimary: '#1677ff', borderRadius: 8, fontFamily: 'Inter' },
  algorithm: theme.defaultAlgorithm /* or theme.darkAlgorithm / compactAlgorithm */ }}>
  <AntApp>{/* app */}</AntApp>
</ConfigProvider>
```

## Theme it to a brand
Design tokens (`token`) for globals, `components: { Button: { … } }` for per-component tokens. `compactAlgorithm` for dense back-office screens.

## Agent tips
- Read `https://ant.design/llms.txt` (and `llms-full.txt`) — official, per-component markdown docs.
- For admin apps use ProComponents (`@ant-design/pro-components`): ProTable, ProForm, ProLayout save a lot of code.
- Use `Form` with `rules` for validation rather than custom state.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

|---|---|
| Official MCP server (agent can query components/docs live) | 0/20 |
| llms.txt on the docs site | 15/15 |

```bash

```

## Setup
```scss
// index.scss
@use '@carbon/react';
```
```tsx
import { Theme, Button } from '@carbon/react';
<Theme theme="white">{/* white | g10 | g90 | g100 */}</Theme>
```

## Theme it to a brand
Carbon is intentionally opinionated; customise via Sass theme tokens (`@use '@carbon/react/scss/themes' with (...)`) and `@carbon/styles` token overrides, not ad-hoc CSS.

## Agent tips
- Tokens are published as `@carbon/themes` / `@carbon/colors` packages (JSON + Sass).
- Use the UI Shell components (`Header`, `SideNav`) for app chrome and `DataTable` for tables.
- Web Components version: `@carbon/web-components`.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.

5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

# Flutter Material 3

> Default choice for Flutter apps: Material 3 widgets ship with the SDK.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tier | **recommended** |
| AI-readiness | **40/100** |
| Maintainer | Google (org-backed) |
| Platforms | ios, android, web, desktop |
| Frameworks | flutter |
| Styling | native |
| Good for | mobile, cross-platform, consumer |
| License | BSD-3-Clause |
| GitHub stars | 181.1k |
| Last activity | 2026-11-05 |
| Docs | https://docs.flutter.dev/ui/design/material |
| Source | https://github.com/flutter/flutter |

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://docs.flutter.dev/llms.txt
- MCP server: none found
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/HEAD/.agents/agents/reidbaker-agent/skills/code-review/SKILL.md


## Install
Ships with the Flutter SDK — no package needed. `flutter create my_app`.

## Setup
```dart
MaterialApp(
  theme: ThemeData(colorScheme: ColorScheme.fromSeed(seedColor: const Color(0xFF4F46E5)), useMaterial3: true),
  darkTheme: ThemeData(colorScheme: ColorScheme.fromSeed(seedColor: const Color(0xFF4F46E5), brightness: Brightness.dark)),
  home: const HomePage(),
);
```

## Agent tips
- One seed colour generates the full M3 palette; customise `textTheme` with `google_fonts`.
- Use `Cupertino*` widgets or `.adaptive` constructors where iOS fidelity matters.
- The Dart & Flutter MCP server (`dart mcp-server`, Dart SDK 3.9+) lets agents analyse, run and hot-reload the app.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.


## Agent tips
- Read https://ui.lobehub.com/llms.txt first — it indexes the official docs in markdown.
- Design tokens live in the repo (e.g. `docs/design-tokens/boardCss.ts`); map brand colours/typography onto these rather than hard-coding values.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

| | |

## AI resources (use these first)
- llms.txt: not published
- **MCP server:**
  - in-repo package: https://github.com/primefaces/primevue/tree/HEAD/packages/mcp (see its README for setup)
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/primefaces/primevue/blob/HEAD/apps/showcase/server/assets/llms/llms-full.txt


## Install
```bash
npm install primevue @primeuix/themes primeicons
```

## Setup
```ts
import PrimeVue from 'primevue/config';
import Aura from '@primeuix/themes/aura';
app.use(PrimeVue, { theme: { preset: Aura, options: { darkModeSelector: '.dark' } } });
```

## Theme it to a brand
`definePreset(Aura, { semantic: { primary: { 50: '{indigo.50}', …, 950: '{indigo.950}' } } })`. Tailwind users can use unstyled mode + the Tailwind preset.

## Agent tips
- The PrimeVue repo ships an MCP package (`packages/mcp`); see docs for setup. Same model for PrimeNG and PrimeReact.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Install
```bash
npm install @cloudscape-design/components @cloudscape-design/global-styles
```

## Setup
```tsx
import '@cloudscape-design/global-styles/index.css';
import { AppLayout, ContentLayout, Header, Table } from '@cloudscape-design/components';
```
Dark mode / density: `applyMode(Mode.Dark)`, `applyDensity(Density.Compact)` from `@cloudscape-design/global-styles`.

## Theme it to a brand
Limited by design: `applyTheme({ theme: { tokens: { colorBackgroundButtonPrimaryDefault: '#…' } } })` from `@cloudscape-design/components/theming`.

## Agent tips
- Use the documented **patterns** (Create resource, Table view, Dashboard) — they map one-to-one to components.
- `@cloudscape-design/board-components` for drag-and-drop dashboards; `@cloudscape-design/chart-components` for charts.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

# Naive UI

> Naive UI by TuSimple.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tier | **recommended** |
| AI-readiness | **45/100** |
| Maintainer | TuSimple |
| Platforms | web |
| Frameworks | vue |
| Styling | css-in-js |
| Good for | admin, dashboard |
| License | MIT |
| GitHub stars | 18.6k |
| npm weekly downloads | 194.8k (`naive-ui`) |
| Last activity | 2026-10-05 |
| Docs | https://www.naiveui.com |
| Source | https://github.com/tusen-ai/naive-ui |

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://www.naiveui.com/llms.txt
- **llms-full.txt:** https://www.naiveui.com/llms-full.txt
- MCP server: none found
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/tusen-ai/naive-ui/blob/HEAD/AGENTS.md

## Consider an alternative if
- you need zero-runtime styling or heavy React Server Components use — check the docs for RSC support.

## Install
```bash
npm install naive-ui
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://www.naiveui.com

## Agent tips
- Read https://www.naiveui.com/llms.txt first — it indexes the official docs in markdown.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Score breakdown
| Capability | Points |
|---|---|
| Official MCP server (agent can query components/docs live) | 0/20 |
| llms.txt on the docs site | 15/15 |
| llms-full.txt (whole docs as one markdown file) | 5/5 |
| Machine-readable design tokens in the repo | 0/15 |
| Typed component API (TypeScript / Swift / Kotlin / Dart / C#) | 10/10 |
| Registry / CLI install of component source (e.g. shadcn registry) | 0/10 |
| Agent instructions in the repo (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, cursor rules, skills) | 5/5 |
| Storybook / live, inspectable examples | 0/5 |
| Figma Code Connect (design ↔ code mapping) | 0/5 |
| Accessibility guidance shipped with the source | 5/5 |
| Dedicated documentation site | 5/5 |

Quality gate: activity **active**; traction via stars, npm.

5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

    ```json

    ```

- the project does not use (or cannot add) Tailwind CSS.

## Install
```bash
npm i -D @spartan-ng/cli
ng g @spartan-ng/cli:init
ng g @spartan-ng/cli:ui button       # adds helm (styled) + brain (headless) parts
```

## How it works
shadcn model for Angular: `brain` = accessible headless primitives (npm), `helm` = Tailwind-styled source copied into your repo.

## Agent tips
- MCP server: `@spartan-ng/mcp`. Theme with the same CSS variables model as shadcn/ui.

## Build checklist (any system)

5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

```bash
npm install @stackoverflow/stacks
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://stackoverflow.design

## Agent tips
- Read https://stackoverflow.design/llms.txt first — it indexes the official docs in markdown.
- Design tokens live in the repo (e.g. `packages/stacks-email/src/lib/tokens.ts`); map brand colours/typography onto these rather than hard-coding values.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## AI resources (use these first)
- **llms.txt:** https://www.infragistics.com/llms.txt
- **llms-full.txt:** https://www.infragistics.com/llms-full.txt
- MCP server: none found
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/IgniteUI/igniteui-webcomponents/blob/HEAD/.agents/skills/add-component-property/SKILL.md


## Install
```bash
npm install igniteui-webcomponents
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://www.infragistics.com/products/ignite-ui-web-components

## Agent tips
- Read https://www.infragistics.com/llms.txt first — it indexes the official docs in markdown.
- Web components work in any framework; in React 19+ they can be used directly, older React may need wrappers.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/shoelace-style/webawesome/blob/HEAD/packages/webawesome/CLAUDE.md


## Install
```html
<!-- CDN (free tier) -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://ka-f.webawesome.com/webawesome@<version>/styles/webawesome.css">
<script type="module" src="https://ka-f.webawesome.com/webawesome@<version>/webawesome.loader.js"></script>
```
or `npm install @awesome.me/webawesome`.

## How it works
Framework-agnostic web components (`<wa-button variant="brand">`) — successor to Shoelace. Works in React, Vue, Svelte, Angular or plain HTML.

## Theme it to a brand
Pick a theme class and override CSS custom properties (`--wa-color-brand-…`, `--wa-border-radius-scale`).

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://jetbrains.github.io/ring-ui/

## Agent tips
- Design tokens live in the repo (e.g. `src/global/variables.css`); map brand colours/typography onto these rather than hard-coding values.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- MCP server: none found

## Install
```bash
npm install @gravity-ui/uikit
# optional: @gravity-ui/navigation @gravity-ui/date-components @gravity-ui/charts @gravity-ui/icons
```

## Setup
```tsx
import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/fonts.css';
import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css';
import { ThemeProvider } from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
<ThemeProvider theme="light">{/* light | dark | light-hc | dark-hc */}</ThemeProvider>
```

## Theme it to a brand
Override CSS variables (`--g-color-base-brand`, `--g-color-text-brand`, …) per theme class (`.g-root_theme_light`). The online Themer at gravity-ui.com generates them.

## Agent tips
- `@gravity-ui/navigation` gives a ready AsideHeader/app shell for consoles.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Score breakdown

> Primer ViewComponents by GitHub.

| Last activity | 2026-11-02 |
| Docs | https://primer.style/view-components |
| Source | https://github.com/primer/view_components |

## AI resources (use these first)
- llms.txt: not published
- **MCP server:**
  - npm package `@primer/mcp`
    ```json
    {"mcpServers":{"primer-view-components":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@primer/mcp"]}}}
    ```
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/primer/view_components/blob/HEAD/.github/copilot-instructions.md

## Consider an alternative if
- you are not building inside the rails ecosystem — its visual language signals that brand.

## Install
```bash
npm install @primer/view-components
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://primer.style/view-components

## Agent tips
- Connect the MCP server listed above before writing code; use it to look up components and props.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.

2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## AI resources (use these first)
- llms.txt: not published
- MCP server: none found

## Consider an alternative if
- you rely on agent tooling — this system has few machine-readable resources, so agents will rely on general knowledge and the docs site.

## Install
```kotlin
// build.gradle.kts
implementation(platform("androidx.compose:compose-bom:<latest>"))
implementation("androidx.compose.material3:material3")
```

## Setup
```kotlin
MaterialTheme(colorScheme = if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) darkScheme else lightScheme, typography = AppTypography) { App() }
```
Generate `lightScheme`/`darkScheme` and typography from a brand colour with Material Theme Builder (exports Compose code). Support dynamic colour on Android 12+ with `dynamicLightColorScheme(context)`.

## Agent tips
- Use `Scaffold`, `TopAppBar`, `NavigationBar`/`NavigationSuiteScaffold` for adaptive layouts.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines + SwiftUI

> Native iOS / macOS apps: SwiftUI system components follow the HIG for free.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tier | **recommended** |
| AI-readiness | **15/100** |
| Maintainer | Apple (org-backed) |
| Platforms | ios, ipados, macos, watchos, visionos |
| Frameworks | swiftui, uikit |
| Styling | native |
| Good for | mobile, consumer, apple-ecosystem |
| License | — |
| GitHub stars | — |
| Last activity | — |
| Docs | https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines |

## AI resources (use these first)
- llms.txt: not published
- MCP server: none found

## Consider an alternative if
- you are not building inside the apple ecosystem — its visual language signals that brand.
- you rely on agent tooling — this system has few machine-readable resources, so agents will rely on general knowledge and the docs site.

## Install
Built into Xcode / SwiftUI — no dependency.

## Setup
Use system components and styles so the HIG is followed automatically: `NavigationStack`, `TabView`, `List`, `Form`, `.toolbar`, `.searchable`, `Button(...).buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)`, semantic colours (`Color.primary`, `.secondary`, `Color(.systemBackground)`), Dynamic Type text styles (`.font(.headline)`), SF Symbols.

## Theme it to a brand
Set `.tint(Color("Brand"))` at the root and define colours in the asset catalog with light/dark variants. Avoid fixed font sizes and custom navigation chrome.

## Agent tips
- Check Apple's HIG page for the component before inventing a pattern.
- Test Dynamic Type, Dark Mode and VoiceOver in previews (`#Preview` with `.environment(\.dynamicTypeSize, .accessibility3)`).

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

```tsx
import '@radix-ui/themes/styles.css';
import { Theme } from '@radix-ui/themes';
<Theme accentColor="indigo" grayColor="slate" radius="medium" scaling="100%">{/* app */}</Theme>
```

## Agent tips
- Layout with `Flex`, `Grid`, `Box`, `Container`, `Section` and their responsive props; no Tailwind needed.
- Theme panel (`<ThemePanel />`) helps pick settings during development; remove before shipping.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Install
```bash
ng add @angular/material
```

## Theme it to a brand
```scss
@use '@angular/material' as mat;
html { @include mat.theme((color: (primary: mat.$violet-palette, theme-type: light), typography: Inter, density: 0)); }
```
Customise further with `mat.<component>-overrides(...)` mixins and the generated `--mat-sys-*` CSS variables.

## Agent tips
- Use the CDK (`@angular/cdk`) for overlays, drag & drop and virtual scroll before reaching for third-party libraries.
- Prefer standalone component imports (`MatButtonModule` etc.) per component.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.

5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.

```bash

```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://www.skeleton.dev

## Agent tips
- Read https://www.skeleton.dev/llms.txt first — it indexes the official docs in markdown.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.


## Agent tips
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

# AI Elements

> Chat, agent and AI-assistant interfaces (messages, prompt input, reasoning, tool calls) on shadcn/ui + AI SDK.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tier | **solid** |
| AI-readiness | **30/100** |
| Maintainer | Vercel (org-backed) |
| Platforms | web |
| Frameworks | react |
| Styling | tailwind |
| Good for | ai-app, chat, saas |
| License | NOASSERTION |
| GitHub stars | 2.5k |
| npm weekly downloads | 152.3k (`ai-elements`) |
| Last activity | 2026-10-14 |
| Docs | https://ai-sdk.dev/elements |
| Source | https://github.com/vercel/ai-elements |

## AI resources (use these first)
- llms.txt: not published
- MCP server: none found
- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/vercel/ai-elements/blob/HEAD/.claude/CLAUDE.md

## Consider an alternative if
- the project does not use (or cannot add) Tailwind CSS.

## Install
```bash
npx ai-elements@latest            # or: npx shadcn@latest add https://registry.ai-sdk.dev/all.json
```
Requires a shadcn/ui setup (Tailwind + CSS variables) and the Vercel AI SDK (`npm install ai @ai-sdk/react`).

## What you get
`Conversation`, `Message`, `PromptInput`, `Response` (streaming markdown), `Reasoning`, `Tool`, `Sources`, `CodeBlock`, `Suggestion`, … as owned source in your repo.

## Agent tips
- Pair with `useChat` from `@ai-sdk/react`; components accept the AI SDK's message parts directly.
- Pick this *with* a base system (usually shadcn/ui), not instead of one.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Build checklist (any system)

5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.
