Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://flowbite-react.com

## Agent tips
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- you rely on agent tooling — this system has few machine-readable resources, so agents will rely on general knowledge and the docs site.

## Install
```bash
flutter pub add macos_ui
```

## Agent tips
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- you rely on agent tooling — this system has few machine-readable resources, so agents will rely on general knowledge and the docs site.

## Install
```bash
npm install react-md
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://react-md.dev

## Agent tips
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- **Agent/contributor docs in repo:** https://github.com/pixiv/charcoal/blob/HEAD/skills/choosing-charcoal-styling/SKILL.md

- you rely on agent tooling — this system has few machine-readable resources, so agents will rely on general knowledge and the docs site.

## Install
```bash
npm install @charcoal-ui/react
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://pixiv.github.io/charcoal/

## Agent tips
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## AI resources (use these first)
- llms.txt: not published
- MCP server: none found

## Consider an alternative if
- you rely on agent tooling — this system has few machine-readable resources, so agents will rely on general knowledge and the docs site.

## Install
```bash
npm install @patternfly/elements
```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://patternflyelements.org

## Agent tips
- Web components work in any framework; in React 19+ they can be used directly, older React may need wrappers.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

# GOV.UK Design System

|---|---|

## AI resources (use these first)
- llms.txt: not published
- MCP server: none found

## Consider an alternative if
- you are building a commercial or non-government product — government systems are designed (and sometimes licensed) for public services.
- you rely on agent tooling — this system has few machine-readable resources, so agents will rely on general knowledge and the docs site.

## Install
```bash
npm install govuk-frontend
```
Use the Nunjucks macros (`{{ govukButton({ text: "Continue" }) }}`) or copy the HTML from each component page. Prototype Kit for rapid prototyping: `npx govuk-prototype-kit create`.

## Agent tips
- Follow the **patterns** (question pages, check answers, confirmation) — they encode tested UX for transactional services.
- Brand customisation is intentionally not supported for GOV.UK services; for non-GOV.UK products use the government system of your own country, or USWDS (more themeable).

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

```bash

```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://ec.europa.eu/component-library/

## Agent tips
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.

## Install
```bash

```
Then follow the framework setup in the official getting-started guide: https://devui.design

## Agent tips
- Design tokens live in the repo (e.g. `devui/design-token/animation/demo/animation-design.component.ts`); map brand colours/typography onto these rather than hard-coding values.
- Use the system's own layout, form and feedback components before adding third-party UI libraries.

## Build checklist (any system)
1. **Install & provider** — follow the install section exactly for the detected framework and version.
2. **Brand → tokens** — set primary/neutral colours, radius, font family and density through the system's theme/tokens API, once, at the root. No hard-coded hex values in components.
3. **App shell first** — build navigation, header and page layout from the system's shell/layout components.
4. **Screens from components** — map each screen of the product idea to existing components and patterns (tables, forms, dialogs, empty states). Only write a custom component when nothing fits, and build it from the system's primitives and tokens.
5. **States** — loading, empty, error and success states for every data view, using the system's skeleton/alert/toast components.
6. **Accessibility** — keep the system's semantics (labels, roles, focus management); check keyboard navigation and colour contrast after theming.
7. **Dark mode & responsiveness** — enable the system's colour-scheme support; check at phone and desktop widths.
8. **Verify** — run the app, click through every screen, fix console errors and type errors.
